answer: Each identity registers one marble shipment and locks a 90-credit bond plus a 35-credit assay fee, 125 per identity. A prism table prices marble by weighed grade, not by self-declaration. An auditor re-weighs it and checks the grade; a mismatch burns the bond. The kth fake still needs its own shipment, bond and assay, so 1,000 fakes cost 125,000 credits with no bulk discount, while an honest agent pays 125 once. A rented shipment fails: its number already sits in the register, and the pulse check pairing each number with one delivery timestamp exposes the duplicate and burns both bonds.
